items.h: Haymitch Gets His Origin Story as Hunger Games Returns to Theaters
items.sum: Sunrise on the Reaping is in theaters, with trackers betting it opens bigger than any Hunger Games film in a decade.

items.h: Kubrick: A Full Retrospective Screens in Astoria Through Dec. 27
items.sum: The Museum of the Moving Image's Stanley Kubrick retrospective runs at the Redstone Theater in Astoria through December 27, timed to a new Criterion box set.

items.h: Sense & the City Invites Visitors to Taste, Touch and Hear New York
items.sum: At City Lore Gallery in the East Village, the show runs on weekends from noon to 6 p.m. through January 18, 2027, with admission at no charge.

items.h: Macy's Unveils Eight New Floats for Its 100th Thanksgiving Parade
items.sum: Eight new floats, including a Tony Sarg marionette tribute, were shown at Macy's Parade Studio in New Jersey.

items.h: Architects of Liberation at MoMA: Modernism in Western Africa
items.sum: On view on the third floor of MoMA's Robert B. Menschel Galleries through January 2, 2027, with about 400 objects from seven countries.

items.h: Handel's Messiah Returns to Carnegie Hall on Dec. 21
items.sum: Monday, December 21 at 7 p.m. in Stern Auditorium at Carnegie Hall in Midtown, with soloists Jen Zetlan, Daniel Moody, Brian Giebler and Jonathan Woody.

items.h: Saint-Saëns's Samson et Dalila Comes to the Met on December 18
items.sum: The Metropolitan Opera lists the Friday evening performance at 7 p.m. in its December season.

items.h: Kevin Puts's Bassoon Concerto Gets Its World Premiere at Geffen Hall
items.sum: Santtu-Matias Rouvali leads the New York Philharmonic at the Wu Tsai Theater on Nov. 25, 27 and 28 and Dec. 1 at 7:30 p.m., with bassoonist Judith LeClair.

items.h: It's a Wonderful Life: A Live Radio Play Opens at the Broadhurst
items.sum: Opening night is tonight at the Broadhurst Theatre, with a limited run through January 3, 2027.

items.h: Harry Potter in Concert With the New York Philharmonic
items.sum: Sunday, December 20 at 2 PM at David Geffen Hall, with the John Williams score performed live.

items.h: Voyager 1 Is Now One Light-Day From Earth
items.sum: After more than 49 years in flight, NASA's farthest spacecraft has crossed a distance light needs a full day to travel.

items.h: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol Aim at Office Work, for Less
items.sum: OpenAI's two new models promise better documents, code and design work at lower prices, as the race with Anthropic and Google tightens.

items.h: Anthropic Lands on Nasdaq With the Largest IPO on Record
items.sum: The Claude maker priced shares at $83, raised about $81 billion and opened its first trading day near $111.

items.h: Xpeng Puts Its Iron Humanoid on Stage Wednesday. The Clock Is Ticking
items.sum: The Chinese EV maker's AI Day on Nov. 25 is its last big show before its own deadline to mass-produce a walking robot.

items.h: The Fockers Crash Thanksgiving, Up Against Disney and Haymitch
items.sum: Focker-In-Law opens Wednesday against Disney's Hexed and a second weekend of the new Hunger Games.

items.h: SOMBR Closes Two Nights at Madison Square Garden Tonight
items.sum: The second of two Madison Square Garden nights, with Dove Cameron and Hannah Jadagu.

items.h: Waymo Takes the Exit: Robotaxis Pulled Off Highways in Five Metros
items.sum: After California called its driverless highway runs a public safety hazard, Waymo stopped highway rides everywhere it offered them, with no restart date.

items.h: The Chats Bring Half Cut to Seattle, Boston and Brooklyn
items.sum: The Australian punks drop their third album in March, then play 30 North American club dates with Chain Whip and Gymshorts.

items.h: New York Today and Tonight: SOMBR, Gnarls Barkley and Glassjaw
items.sum: Tuesday picks: an arena closer, a Carnegie Hall concert and a full club list.

items.h: Fusion Has Record Money. It Still Needs $80 Billion More.
items.sum: A new global outlook counts more fusion machines and more private cash than ever, and a long, expensive road before any of it lights your kitchen.

items.h: Cliff Booth Is Back, and He Only Plays in IMAX for Two Weeks
items.sum: David Fincher directs Brad Pitt in a Quentin Tarantino script that picks up eight years after Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, opening in IMAX Wednesday.
